items.title: Formal smoothness of an extension of discrete valuation rings is inherited by finite extensions of the fraction field
items.author: The Stacks Project Authors
items.work: Stacks Project, chapter more-algebra.tex (More on Algebra)
items.source_version: Stacks Project source tree, file more-algebra.tex, corpus local snapshot 20261012
items.difficulty_reason: The lemma takes an extension A -> B of discrete valuation rings with fraction fields K in L, assumes A -> B formally smooth in the m_B-adic topology, and asserts that for any finite extension K_1/K, with L_1 = L tensor_K K_1, B_1 = B tensor_A A_1, and the extensions (A_1)_{m_i} in (B_1)_{m_ij} of the construction remark, each such extension is formally smooth in the m_ij-adic topology (source lines 34005-34014). The proof works through the equivalence of the formally smooth characterisation for extensions of discrete valuation rings, used without further mention (proof lines 34016-34017). Let pi in A and pi_i in (A_1)_{m_i} be uniformizers. Because kappa_A in kappa_B is separable, the ring (B tensor_A (A_1)_{m_i}) / pi_i (B tensor_A (A_1)_{m_i}), rewritten as B/piB tensor_{A/piA} (A_1)_{m_i}/pi_i(A_1)_{m_i}, is a product of fields each separable over kappa_{m_i} (proof lines 34018-34024). Hence pi_i is a nonzerodivisor in B tensor_A (A_1)_{m_i} and the quotient by it is a product of fields (proof lines 34025-34026). It follows that B tensor_A A_1 is a Dedekind domain, in particular reduced, so the inclusion B tensor_A A_1 in B_1 is an equality, which is what was to be shown (proof lines 34027-34028). The non-routine content is the rewriting of the residue ring as a tensor product of residue fields and the use of separability of the residue extension to read off the nonzerodivisor property; the final step is the identification of B_1 with the tensor product via the Dedekind property.
